Definition: from G5368; amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity:--Philetus.
BiblicalUsage: Philetus is a man Paul names as an opposer of the faith, whose word eats like a canker. He and Hymenaeus have erred concerning the truth, saying that the resurrection is past already, and they overthrow the faith of some.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Philetus is remembered as a warning: wrong teaching spreads like a canker, and a resurrection moved into the past steals hope from the present.
